key_insight: Reliable a posteriori error estimators quantify finite element errors in evolution equations with memory without exponential growth in time, while remaining uniformly bounded across the fractional-kernel parameter range.
engineering_relevance: These estimators can guide adaptive simulation of memory-dependent dynamics transitioning between diffusion and wave propagation.
method: Time-dependent finite element spaces with backward Euler time stepping and memory quadrature.
Elliptic reconstruction for optimal spatial error estimates.
Memory-lag analysis preserving convolution cancellation for first-order temporal estimation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on a convex domain validate the estimates, and space-time adaptivity is demonstrated on an L-shaped domain with a corner singularity and two temporal layers.
watch_item: The stated theory assumes convex polygonal or polyhedral domains; the nonconvex L-shaped example is an adaptive demonstration.
paper_title: A Posteriori Error Analysis of Finite Element Approximation to an Evolution Equation with a Positive-Type Memory Term
